module_title: Monsoon Mechanisms, Retreating Winds, and Local Storms
introduction: At this level, we explore the thermal theory behind wind reversal, the phenomenon of the retreating monsoon, and the various pre-monsoon local showers that affect agriculture.

core_concepts.title: Thermal Concept (Halley's Theory)
core_concepts.description: During summer, the Indian landmass heats up intensely, creating an intense Low-Pressure area. The Indian Ocean remains relatively cool, maintaining High-Pressure. Winds naturally blow from High Pressure (Sea) to Low Pressure (Land), bringing moisture.

core_concepts.title: Retreating Monsoon (North-East Monsoon)
core_concepts.description: During October-November, as the land cools down, the winds reverse and start blowing from Land to Sea (North-East direction). These winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and cause heavy winter rainfall specifically on the 'Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu)'.

core_concepts.title: El Niño
core_concepts.description: A periodic warming of the Pacific Ocean near the coast of Peru. Whenever an El Niño event occurs, the Indian monsoon becomes 'Weak', leading to deficient rainfall and potential droughts in India.

core_concepts.title: La Niña
core_concepts.description: The exact opposite of El Niño, characterized by unusual cooling of the Pacific Ocean. La Niña is highly favorable for the Indian monsoon, often resulting in 'Above Normal' rainfall and floods.

important_entities.name: Mango Showers
important_entities.significance: Occurring in May in Kerala and Karnataka, these local pre-monsoon rains help in the early ripening of mangoes, hence the name.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Winter rain in North-West India (Punjab, Delhi) is caused by 'Western Disturbances'. Winter rain in South India (Tamil Nadu) is caused by the 'Retreating / North-East Monsoon'. Do not mix them up!

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Kal Baisakhi (Doom/Destruction) = West Bengal/Assam. Cherry Blossom / Coffee Showers (Bloom) = Karnataka.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions are common for local storms: Kal Baisakhi -> West Bengal; Mango Showers -> Kerala; Cherry Blossom -> Karnataka.
A guaranteed question: Which coast receives maximum rainfall during winter? Answer: Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu).
